props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted spin · offline render
props.title: A Picture Off to the Side

B01.capture_spec: C01 (scene c01): picture 512, blob 448 with 01-inner-gradient (turned by a script at 0.9 rad/s), shown on a QuadMesh 512 x -512, 31 x 31, with 09-rainbow-wobble. 18 s, 30 fps, Forward+.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'A Picture Off to the Side' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render on the cream stage: the teal blob turns, rainbow stripes slide across it, and the whole picture ripples like cloth. Nothing is labelled yet; the effect is the hook.
B01.motion_claim: The blob turns, the stripes slide and the picture ripples the whole time.
B01.runner_up: manim drawing of the finished look
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of an effect; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: Two frames on the cream stage. Right: a large outline rectangle labelled 'screen', empty. Left: a smaller dashed square labelled 'SubViewport'. A teal blob fades into the small square, then a text glyph 'Aa', a small button outline and a three-line cube join it. The screen stays empty the whole time. Caption under the square: 'off-screen: drawn, not shown directly'; a one-line definition on the square: 'draws its children into a picture of its own'.
B02.motion_claim: Children drop into the small square one by one while the screen frame stays empty.

show.event: screen frame and the SubViewport square
blob lands inside the square; the screen stays empty
text, button and cube join it

B02.why: The claim is 'drawn, but not shown': a box that fills while the screen stays empty says it with motion.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · texture handed over at 7 s · scripted

B03.capture_spec: C02 (scene c02): picture 512 opaque (clear colour #A8A090), blob 448, a Sprite2D whose texture is empty until 7.0 s, then `display.texture = sub.get_texture()`. 14 s, 30 fps, Forward+. Verified (run-7a): the centre is the stage (0.851, 0.835, 0.792) at 6 s and the teal blob (0.373, 0.639, 0.569) in the clear-coloured box at 8.5 s.
B03.visual_intent: Code card with the one real line at left; at right a real Godot window on the cream stage: empty for seven seconds, then the picture appears (a teal blob in a mid-grey box, the viewport's clear colour) at the moment the line runs.
B03.motion_claim: The stage is empty until the texture is handed over, then the picture appears.
B03.runner_up: manim: a drawn box feeding a screen
B03.why: Nothing on screen, then the picture on the very line that makes it appear, is the claim as a cause and an effect.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 editor · three real frames · scripted editor session

B04.capture_spec: E1-1, E2-1, E2-4: three static editor frames of the scratch project, recorded by the series' editor driver from this film's state script (evidence/planning-checks/editor-driver/state-scripts/subviewports-E1.json, run-15; the -wide variant widens the Inspector so long labels read in full). The clicks themselves are not shown, only the resulting states; the menu frame is the real Texture slot menu.
B04.visual_intent: Three real frames of the whole Godot editor window, cross-dissolving: (1) subviewports_E1-1_subviewport-size: Scene dock Main > SubViewport > Sprite2D, Display; the SubViewport selected; the Inspector with its picture preview and Size 512 x 512, ring on Size; (2) subviewports_E2-1_texture-dropdown-new-viewporttexture: the Display sprite's Texture slot menu open (a Search box, the heading New, ViewportTexture highlighted), ring on ViewportTexture; (3) subviewports_E2-4_viewport-path-set: the ViewportTexture with Viewport Path = SubViewport, ring on Viewport Path.
B04.motion_claim: The ring moves slot to slot as the voice names each step.

show.event: the Texture slot's menu is open

B04.why: Real editor frames are the first rung of SHOW-THE-THING; every label on them was read from the editor itself (planning evidence).

B05.visual_intent: Left: a code card with five real lines (monospace): var sub := SubViewport.new() / sub.size = Vector2i(512, 512) / add_child(sub) / sub.add_child(inner_sprite) / display.texture = sub.get_texture(). Right: a diagram that builds with the focused line: a small tree 'Main' on top, a dashed box, a screen frame at the lower right. Line 1 draws the dashed box ('sub'); line 2 writes '512 x 512' along its edges; line 3 hooks it under 'Main'; line 4 drops a teal blob into it; line 5 draws an arrow from the box to a display sprite on the screen, and the blob appears on the screen.
B05.motion_claim: Each line, when focused, makes its piece appear on the right.

show.event: line 5: the arrow and the picture on screen

B05.why: A line and its consequence appear together; only a drawing built line by line shows that each line adds one piece.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted: Filter switches at 12.5 s
props.caption: resolution: how many pixels the picture holds

B06.capture_spec: C03 (scene c03): two opaque viewports, 512 and 128 px (blob drawn natively at each size), displays at x = 100 and x = 668, the right at scale 4; Filter Linear until 12.5 s (on the words "Filter to Nearest"), then Nearest. 19 s, Forward+. Verified (run-7a): soft edge 8 pixels on the blob row with Linear at 7 s, 0 with Nearest at 14 s, runs 104 / 304 / 104 (multiples of 4).
B06.visual_intent: Two real displays of the same blob, both 512 px across on the stage: left a 512 px picture drawn 1:1 (crisp), right a 128 px picture drawn 4x (soft with the Linear filter). Partway, the right display's Filter switches to Nearest and the soft edge turns into hard blocks.
B06.motion_claim: The right picture is soft, then snaps into crisp blocks when the filter changes.

show.event: 512 px and 128 px pictures side by side
Filter: Nearest; the edge turns into blocks

B06.why: The softness and the blocks are the claim; only the real render shows what the engine does to a small picture.

props.caption: origin: where the picture's coordinates start, (0, 0)

B07.capture_spec: C04a (scene c04a): opaque picture 512, blob 448 centred at (256, 256), stays in the middle while the voice explains the origin, slides to (0, 0) between 6.4 s and 8.6 s (on "placed at zero, zero"), then holds; 16 s, Forward+. Verified (run-7a): 55,202 teal and 1,546 eye pixels at 5 s; at (0, 0) from 8.6 s the picture holds 14,187 teal pixels = 25.7 % of the whole blob and 0 eye pixels.
B07.visual_intent: A real display of a 512 px picture (mid-grey box). The blob starts in the middle, slides to the top-left corner and settles there: only its bottom-right quarter is in the picture and its eyes are gone. A terracotta ring marks the corner; a readout 'origin (0, 0)'.
B07.motion_claim: The blob slides into the corner and three quarters of it vanish, eyes first.

show.event: the blob slides into the corner

B07.runner_up: manim: axes with a clipped sprite
B07.why: The clipping is the claim; the real picture shows exactly which part survives.

B08.capture_spec: C04b (scene c04b): opaque picture 512, blob slides from (0, 0) to (256, 256) between 0.3 s and 3.3 s, holds, then to x = 560 between 4.0 s and 7.0 s; 16 s, Forward+. Verified (run-7a): 14,187 teal pixels at 0.2 s, 55,202 in the middle at 3.7 s, 15,470 when the blob is cut by the right edge at 9 s and at the end (centre at x = 560).
B08.visual_intent: The same display. The blob slides from the corner to the middle (all of it appears), holds, then slides off the right edge and is cut off sharply at the picture's edge. Readouts 'all of it' then 'cut off'.
B08.motion_claim: The blob arrives whole in the middle, then is sliced by the picture's right edge.
B08.why: The cut line is the claim; a real picture shows it cut without a seam.

cues.label: Transparent BG: empty parts become see-through

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted: Transparent BG on at 8 s

B09.capture_spec: C05 (scene c05): grid of 2 px lines every 64 px behind the display, opaque picture until 8.0 s then `transparent_bg = true`; 15 s, Forward+. Verified (run-7a): the empty pixel is the clear colour (0.659, 0.627, 0.565) before and the stage (0.851, 0.835, 0.792) after; the picture's empty pixel alpha goes from 1 to 0.
B09.visual_intent: Code card with one line at left; at right the display over a faint grey grid: first the picture's mid-grey box hides the grid, then at the moment the line runs the box vanishes and the grid shows through, leaving only the blob.
B09.motion_claim: The box disappears and the grid behind it shows through.

show.event: Transparent BG on; the box vanishes

B09.why: A box that vanishes to reveal what was behind it is the claim; the grid makes the see-through visible.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted: Blend Mode changes at 10.5 s
props.caption: premultiplied: each color already multiplied by its alpha

B10.capture_spec: C06 (scene c06): picture 512 transparent, glow image (gold, alpha falling to 0 over the outer 45 % of its radius) over the grid; the display uses a CanvasItemMaterial, Blend Mode Mix until 10.5 s then Premultiplied Alpha; 18 s, Forward+. Verified (run-7a, run-5 G1) at ring pixel (807, 360): Mix (0.655, 0.608, 0.490), Premultiplied (0.890, 0.800, 0.576), the glow drawn directly (0.890, 0.796, 0.576).
B10.visual_intent: One real display of a soft gold glow over the faint grid. It starts with Blend Mode Mix: a muddy dark ring surrounds the glow. At the moment the blend mode changes to Premultiplied Alpha the dark ring vanishes and the glow is clean. A terracotta ring marks the dark ring; readouts name the two blend modes.
B10.motion_claim: The dark ring around the glow vanishes the moment the blend mode changes.

show.event: Premultiplied Alpha: the ring is gone

B10.why: The ring that vanishes is the claim; arithmetic would explain it, but the real glow is what a viewer will meet.
